headline: iPhone Ultra could launch in US only at first, per new report
summary: A new report suggests Apple's upcoming iPhone Ultra might have an extremely limited initial rollout, potentially launching exclusively in the US.
details: A new report indicates that Apple's highly anticipated iPhone Ultra could see an extremely limited initial rollout. Sources suggest the device might be available exclusively in the United States at launch, restricting its global availability.

This strategy would mark a significant departure from Apple's typical global release patterns for new iPhone models. Such a move could be aimed at testing market demand or managing supply chain complexities for a premium, potentially higher-priced device.

The report from 9to5Mac, citing unnamed sources, emphasizes the unconfirmed nature of these plans. If true, international customers might face a longer wait before the iPhone Ultra becomes available in their regions.

headline: Microsoft merges Copilot apps into unified 'super app' experience
summary: The move unifies consumer and commercial AI assistants, eliminating duplicate icons and laying groundwork for a future 'super app' with a worldwide rollout starting mid-August.
details: Microsoft is merging its consumer and commercial Copilot AI assistants into a single unified "Microsoft Copilot" app. This update combines Copilot chat and image creation with Microsoft 365 capabilities for work, featuring an updated app icon. It also resolves the issue of duplicate Copilot icons in the system tray or taskbar.

This unification is a technical milestone preparing for a larger "super app" Microsoft plans to launch later this year. The worldwide rollout for mobile and web apps begins in "mid-August," followed by Windows and Mac apps in "mid-September." Some Windows Insiders will see updates this week.

Existing Microsoft Copilot users will transition to the updated version with their chats and content carried over. Microsoft 365 Copilot app users will experience minor navigation changes, the new icon, and access to Copilot chat. Users of both apps will have their content merged into a single updated app, though personal and work data remain separate within it.

Enterprise security, compliance, and government controls remain unchanged. Users can still switch between personal Microsoft accounts and work/school Microsoft Entra ID accounts, with data staying separate. Core Copilot features remain free, though usage limits for the free experience may vary.

Some features will be retired: Podcasts and Deep Research will not be available after August 18th. Group Chat threads, messages, and content will also not be carried over after this date. Other features like Shopping and Copilot Health may be temporarily unavailable during the rollout.
